title: Sugar Snap Pea Pancakes
changes_from_base: Small savoury pancakes made from blanched sugar snaps puréed with milk and cream, bound with egg and a little flour, with coarsely puréed peas folded in; cooked in butter and finished briefly in a 230 °C oven.
summary: Delicate little pancakes made from puréed sugar snap and shelled peas, finished in the oven for a tender, bright green bite.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
ingredients.note: about ¼ tsp; ⅛ tsp in the batter, plus a little to finish

steps.title: Blanch
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230 °C. Bring a lightly salted pan of water to the boil and blanch the 113 g sugar snap peas for 2 min, then chill in iced water and drain; blanch the 75 g shelled peas for about 3 min, chill and drain.

steps.title: Purée
steps.text: Purée the sugar snaps with the 2 tbsp milk and 1 tbsp double cream, pour into a bowl and whisk in the 1 egg.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Sift in the 30 g flour, ½ tsp baking powder, ⅛ tsp sugar and ⅛ tsp salt and whisk to combine, then coarsely purée the shelled peas and fold them in.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Melt 7 g butter in an ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat and drop in tablespoons of batter.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: When the edges are lightly browned, put the pan in the 230 °C oven for 1½ min.

steps.title: Flip
steps.text: Take the pan out, flip the pancakes gently, cook on the hob until lightly browned underneath, then return to the oven for 1 min more.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Drain on kitchen paper and season with salt and pepper, then repeat with the remaining batter and butter.

tips: Chill the peas in iced water straight after blanching to keep their colour bright.
Work in small batches - the pancakes are delicate and best made a few at a time.
Finishing them briefly in the oven helps them cook through without overbrowning.
storage: These are best eaten fresh and warm, straight from the pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
